processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting with solidification in Cu moulds
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Binary Fe-Al alloy melted in an Al2O3 crucible from Fe (99.99% purity, zone-melting purified) and Al (99.999% purity), solidified in Cu moulds to rods usually with 18 mm diameter.

processing_steps.method: none — used in the as-received as-cast condition
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The as-cast polycrystalline alloys were tested without any subsequent heat treatment; the as-cast condition is the baseline state.

structures.overall_structure: Coarse-grained polycrystalline microstructure; the as-cast alloy contained no second phases.

phases_present.phase_name: Fe–Al solid solution (disordered bcc / K-state short-range-order region)

interfaces.phase_evolution: As-cast material: no second phases. Fine thin platelike or rod-like precipitates (believed to be carbides, consistent with up to 80 ppm C) appear on grain boundaries only after slow furnace cooling from 1100 °C or prolonged heat treatments (e.g. 14 days at 320 °C); they are not present in the as-cast state.
interfaces.interface_notes: Grain boundaries of the coarse-grained polycrystal are the only internal interfaces; no second phase at grain boundaries in the as-cast condition. Carbide precipitation on grain boundaries occurs only after heat treatments and its amount decreases with lower C content.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical specimens prepared by turning (turning per DIN 50125)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile testing; tension rate between 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^-2 s^-1.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Tensile stress-strain curve of Fe-11at%Al at room temperature (Fig. 4a)

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical specimens prepared by turning (turning per DIN 50125)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile testing at low temperature; ductile-to-brittle behaviour studied at -100 °C.

ultimate_tensile_strength.value: ≈? (higher than room temperature by about 80 MPa)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Tensile stress-strain curve of Fe-11at%Al at -100 °C (Fig. 4b)

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: 5 × 5 × 10 mm3 compression specimens (surfaces cleansed by grinding)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Yield stress determined as 0.2% proof stress in compression with total straining of at least 5%. Fig. 3 gives yield stress versus Al content for as-cast polycrystals; the linear fit corresponds to a solid-solution hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa over 0–18 at.% Al (specific numeric value at 11 at.% Al not tabulated).

characterization_methods.key_findings: Real Al content of the nominal 11 at.% polycrystal is 10.9 at.% (5.6 wt.-%), with 60 wt.ppm C and 80 wt.ppm Si.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens etched by an alcoholic 10% nitric acid solution
characterization_methods.key_findings: Polycrystalline alloys show a coarse grain structure with grain sizes of the order of 1 mm; the as-cast alloys contained no second phases.

characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray diffraction (EDX)
characterization_methods.purpose: Studying fracture surfaces and qualitative precipitate analysis
characterization_methods.key_findings: SEM used for fracture-surface study of the tested polycrystalline alloys; EDX used for qualitative precipitate analysis.

unmapped_findings: The yield stress of the polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys (0–18 at.% Al, so including Fe-11%Al) increases linearly with Al content; the interpolating straight lines give a yield-stress increase of 21 MPa per at.% at 10^-2 s^-1 and 23 MPa per at.% at 10^-4 s^-1, corresponding to a solid-solution hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa, which is not sensitive to deformation rate or temperature. [b0032, b0058]
At -100 °C the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength of the polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys are higher than at room temperature by about 80 MPa. [b0038]

Deformation twinning at -100 °C was observed occasionally for Al contents of 11–14% (thus including Fe-11%Al), and in all specimens above 14% Al; at room temperature twinning was found only for the Fe-18%Al alloy. [b0038, b0064]
The Fe-11%Al as-cast alloy did not show low-temperature yield stress drops (yield stress drops were produced only by Fe-4%Al and Fe-6%Al at -100 °C). [b0062]
Impurity content of the nominal-11 at.% polycrystal: C 60 wt.ppm, Si 80 wt.ppm, residual 'other' elements not reported (below the detection limits of Table 1 footnote a). [b0025]

Short-range ordering (controlled by heat treatments below 600 °C) has no major impact on the deformation behaviour; only heat treatments above 600 °C significantly affect the mechanical behaviour of Fe-Al alloys. [b0050, b0051, b0067]
The Fe-11%Al alloy was tested in tension at rates between 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^-2 s^-1 using cylindrical specimens per DIN 50125, and in compression (5 × 5 × 10 mm3) as a 0.2% proof stress. [b0019]
